t: 2815. Max Pair Sum in an Array
o: Group numbers by their largest digit (computable by digit scan; values ≤ 10⁴ so at most 4 digits). Within each group, the best pair sum uses the two largest numbers, so keeping just the group maximum and updating the answer as new values arrive suffices. Example 3: digits are [5,7,7,4,4]; group 7 holds {71,17} → 88 beats group 4's 66.
k: Bucket by largest digit; only the top-two values per bucket matter.
Streaming update: answer = max(answer, stored_best[d] + v) before replacing stored_best[d].

a.n: Approach 1: Hash Map of Group Maxima
a.i: For each number compute its max digit d; if we've seen another number with digit d, candidate sum = stored max + current; then update the stored max for d.
s: Helper to compute the largest digit of a number.
Iterate nums: if d seen, update answer with stored[d] + v; set stored[d] = max(stored[d], v).
Return answer, or −1 if never updated.
a.t: O(n · D) where D ≤ 5 is the digit count — effectively O(n)

a.i: With n ≤ 100, checking all O(n²) pairs and comparing largest digits is perfectly fine and simplest to reason about.
s: Double loop over pairs (i, j), i < j.
If maxdigit(nums[i]) == maxdigit(nums[j]), consider their sum.

w: Use Approach 1 in an interview to show awareness of scaling; Approach 2 is a fine sanity baseline. Pitfall: initialize the answer to −1 and only overwrite on successful pairs. Watch that a pair needs two distinct indices — the streaming update naturally handles this by comparing before overwriting the stored max.
